https://www.barrons.com/articles/qualcomm-stock-plunges-on-gloomy-outlook-1541709683 Qualcomm Stock Plunges on Gloomy Outlook By Nov. 8, 2018 3:41 p.m. ET Order Reprints Text size
Wall Street analysts aren’t too happy about Qualcomm ’s (QCOM) latest guidance.
Late Wednesday, Qualcomm reported better-than-expected fiscal fourth-quarter results but gave a financial forecast below consensus. It projected a sales range of $4.5 billion to $5.3 billion for its fiscal first quarter, compared with the Wall Street average estimate of $5.6 billion, according to FactSet. Bank of America Merrill Lynch analyst Tal Liani reiterated his Neutral rating for Qualcomm shares, citing its recent licensing disagreements with key customers Huawei Technologies and Apple (AAPL).
“While we view Qualcomm’s leadership, opportunities in market adjacencies and 5G potentials positively…the valuation is relatively unattractive and the investment case depends on a licensing resolution, of which the timing is uncertain,” he wrote on Thursday.
Qualcomm’s stock was down 8.5%, to $57.83 on Thursday. Its shares have declined about 9% year to date.
Liani lowered his price target for Qualcomm stock to $67 from $70. Newsletter Sign-up
While acknowledging the company’s weak near-term outlook, Rosenblatt Securities analyst Jun Zhang reiterated his Buy rating for the chipmaker due to the opportunity in 5G, or fifth-generation wireless technology.
“Although Qualcomm’s weak C4Q guidance reflects a Chinese smartphone market slow down, our thesis that Qualcomm will benefit from 5G smartphone trends over the next few years remains unchanged,” he wrote on Thursday.
Zhang noted that 5G phones using Qualcomm technology will launch as early as next year.
The analyst reaffirmed his $70 price target for the company.
